task: Remove the phantom memory agent from the orchestrator capability matrix, add a validator that pins every matrix agent name to a real agent file, and record the two knowledge defects the fix exposed: GENERATOR-FILES.md misclassified src/claude as generated, and both portability gates skip agent trees entirely.

events.content: Verified the premise before editing. .claude/agents/memory.md does not exist, templates/agents/memory.shared.md does not exist, and .claude/skills/memory does. Of 18 orchestrator matrix rows exactly one had no agent file. Lines 8 and 16 of the template list memory under tools_vscode and tools_copilot; those are tool names, not agents, and were left alone.

Read GENERATOR-FILES.md before touching a plugin root, which listed src/claude as a generate_agents.py output. Ran both generators; neither wrote src/claude/orchestrator.md and the phantom row survived. validate_install_parity.py encodes the truth: src/claude has no generator and is hand-maintained, corrected in Issue #2882. Fixed the stale row and moved src/claude into the hand-maintained table.

Caught a self-inflicted plugin self-containment violation by reading. The first draft of the matrix note said every row resolves to a file at .claude/agents/<name>.md. That body is copied into six trees across two plugin roots, so the path is wrong in most of them and dangles for every Copilot installer. Confirmed neither portability gate scans agent files, so nothing would have flagged it. Rewrote the note to name no path.

Wrote the validator with an explicit anti-vacuous guard, having twice this session shipped a scan that narrowed silently and still exited 0. The guard paid for itself on first run: it reported a matrix header with zero parsed rows in two files, because the row pattern matched only bolded names. Widening it surfaced two more phantom memory rows in the agent index tables that the orchestrator-only fix had missed.

The first version of the guard failed the wrong thing. It required every scanned tree to carry a matrix, which fires on correct repositories where a tree holds only agent definitions. Two tests caught it. Narrowed to real degeneration: no matrix anywhere, none in the canonical templates tree, or a header with no rows. The tree-list protection moved into a filesystem-anchored test, because at runtime a tree with no table cannot be told apart from a tree dropped out of the constant.

Proved the validator is not vacuous by running it against a detached origin/main worktree: 8 violations across all 8 sites, versus 0 on this branch. Mutation tested with 10 mutants; the first pass reported 1 survivor which turned out to be a broken mutant whose conditional evaluated to a no-op. Rewrote it as a real shrink of MATRIX_TREES and it was killed by the filesystem-anchored test, which named the five dropped trees.

Enforced one direction only. Every cited name must resolve; an agent file need not appear in any matrix. Twelve shipped agents are absent from the orchestrator table, and adding them is a curation call with a context-budget cost, not an invariant. Recorded the omission in the docstring so it reads as deliberate.

Cited issue #3465 for the agent-tree gate gap rather than filing a duplicate. That issue already carries the per-surface measurement. The rule text adds what the issue lacks: the working practice to follow until the ratchet widens, plus the near-miss from this branch as evidence.

Replaced the hand-written matrix parser with markdown-it-py, already a project dependency. Three adversarial rounds had each found a new spelling the patterns missed; the fourth asked why the code was approximating a documented grammar at all. Frontmatter now parses as YAML rather than by pattern.

Fixed a denial of service the rewrite introduced. safe_load blocks object construction, not resource use: SafeConstructor.flatten_mapping expands a merge key by copying every entry of the aliased mapping, so a 433 byte frontmatter block held the scan for 21.67 seconds. Aliases are refused outright. Zero of 176 shipped blocks use one, and a test pins that.

Made the frontmatter fences agree. The open required exactly three hyphens and a newline while the close tolerated trailing whitespace, so a file opening with a padded fence was not an agent and every matrix row citing it reported that it does not ship. The close search also moved off a hardcoded offset of four, correct only for a bare fence.

Fixed two disagreements between the validator and what a reader sees. A UTF-8 byte order mark made a well-formed agent invisible at both read sites. A degenerate scan printed its errors and then announced that every agent checks out; the exit code was already right, only the summary contradicted it.

Discovered the mutation harness was measuring nothing. It reported 48 of 48 planted defects caught. It copied the tree without .git, a teardown fixture reads the repository HEAD, so the suite died on its first test and the harness read that nonzero exit as a kill. The trigger is the .git strip; the cause is that the harness never ran the unmutated code, so it could not tell a kill from a suite that failed to start.

Added a baseline gate that refuses to report anything unless the unmutated suite is green. Corrected figure: 44 of 53. The nine survivors were real. Six were untested behaviour and are now tested. Three were branches for a table row holding no cell, which the parser cannot produce: measured across 69,847 rows in 3,106 files it never happened, so the branches are gone and the invariant is stated where it is relied upon. 52 of 52 now.

Two assertions in this session could not fail. A pre-flight check walked ast.Assign looking for an annotated assignment and reported zero problems while examining zero things. A guard scanned whole file text for a pattern that only means something inside frontmatter. Both were green and both were empty. The alias test now carries a non-vacuity floor.
Filed #3594 as the correct issue for this work. The PR body cited #3565, which belongs to another PR, so merging would have closed an issue whose work is unfinished.
Adversarial round 6 on a further model family found the new BOM matrix test vacuous; reproduced by reverting the scan-site fix and watching it still pass.
First rewrite was also vacuous: the fixture opened with a heading, so the mark landed there and not on the table. Rewrote against a bare table.
Added two BOM mutants; both killed. Full sweep now 54 of 54 killed, 0 survived, 0 invalid, baseline green.
Re-measured rows on tracked files at 02a4be1c30: 69,785 rows in 3,912 files, 0 cellless. Matches the reviewer exactly; the earlier figure swept untracked scratch.
Re-derived the YAML bomb with merge keys rather than alias lists: depth 8 is 446 bytes and 21.46s. Restated as under 500 bytes and 21.5s with the byte range, since spelling moves the count.
Commit: 02a4be1c30
Retargeted PR #3587 to Fixes #3594 and verified the body no longer contains Fixes #3565.

Fixed the review findings: unreadable markdown now exits 2, active memory-agent references are removed, the Claude-only quality-auditor route is retained, and Copilot skill prose no longer points at an agent it does not ship.

Validation: targeted pytest suite passed with TMPDIR and basetemp under /home/richard/src/GitHub/rjmurillo/pytest-tmp-pr3587; ruff passed; validate_agent_matrix_refs.py returned 0 on the repo; blockquote and invalid-fence ghost probes returned 1; invalid UTF-8 probe returned 2.
